transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I'm here because I've been struggling with eating really huge amounts of food all at once. When it happens, it feels like I completely lose control and just can't stop myself. I really need some help figuring out how to handle this.

After these episodes, do you ever try to make up for the eating by vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot? This will help me understand what kind of eating problem you’re dealing with.
No, I don't do any of those things at all. I have never tried to make myself throw up, use laxatives, fast, or do extreme workouts to make up for what I ate.
How often do these episodes happen, and for about how many months have they been going on?
On average, these episodes happen at least once a week. I've been struggling with this pattern for about two years and two months now.

During these episodes, do you usually eat much more quickly than normal, eat until you feel uncomfortably full, eat when you’re not physically hungry, eat alone because you feel embarrassed, or feel disgusted, depressed, or very guilty afterward?

Yes, I always eat alone because I feel so embarrassed by how much I'm consuming, and I feel deeply disgusted, depressed, and guilty afterward. However, I don't really eat faster than normal, eat until I'm uncomfortably full, or eat when I'm not actually hungry.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["Binge-Eating Disorder"], and based on this conversation the candidate list remains the same. The patient reports recurrent binge episodes with loss of control, occurring at least weekly for over 2 years, marked distress afterward, and no compensatory behaviors such as vomiting, laxatives, fasting, or excessive exercise. The endorsed associated features (eating alone due to embarrassment and feeling disgusted/depressed/guilty afterward) support Binge-Eating Disorder, and the absence of compensatory behaviors makes Bulimia Nervosa unlikely, so the list remains narrowed to Binge-Eating Disorder.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports recurrent episodes of eating unusually large amounts of food with a clear sense of loss of control, occurring at least weekly for over 2 years. Episodes are associated with eating alone due to embarrassment and marked guilt, disgust, and depressed feelings afterward. There are no compensatory behaviors such as vomiting, laxatives, fasting, or excessive exercise, supporting Binge-Eating Disorder.
